description:
src/filenode.rs:1455-1476 (unit test): asserts 'resp["created"].is_object()' and 'resp["notCreated"].is_null()'. MockBackend's create_object (src/lib.rs:366-374) returns 'Ok((Id::from("mock-id-1"), obj))' regardless of input. So the test is asserting:

1. The handler did not fail validation.
2. The handler did call backend.create_object.
3. The handler propagated the backend's Ok response into the created map.

What the test does NOT assert: the inferred nodeType actually reaches the backend. The MockBackend echoes the supplied obj back, so the response will contain nodeType='directory' regardless of whether the handler set it or whether serde's default behavior did.

A stronger test would peek at the obj passed to create_object via a recording MockBackend (capture the argument), then assert capture.last().node_type == NodeType::Directory. As written, the test passes if any branch (handler, serde default, MockBackend) sets nodeType='directory'.

This is a test-quality issue: the test's name suggests it covers handler inference, but the assertion does not isolate the handler from the rest of the pipeline.
title: set_create_directory_without_blobid_infers_directory_type asserts on MockBackend that does not actually create anything
